subject: Follow-up: ACME discovery — performance SLOs & SLA language
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance and SLA workstreams: 

1) Qual requirements we discussed
- Target tail latency: p99 <= 350ms for single-shot generate (50 token avg)
- Streaming: chunked token streaming with ~50ms per-chunk egress target after first token
- Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state 120 req/s with occasional bursts to 400 req/s; planned concurrency per model ~32

2) Measurement clarifications we need from you
- Do you want p95 and p99 included in the SLA or p99-only?
- Any exclusions you expect (maintenance windows, controlled load tests, scheduled deployments)?
- Reporting cadence: weekly dashboards vs. monthly executive report?

3) Next steps
- I attached the draft mutual action plan and initial SLO doc (slo-draft.docx). Please confirm or flag items by Tue (6/16).
- We will produce proposed SLA language that specifies measurement points, exclusions, reporting cadence, and remedies (service credits) — target deliverable 6/18.
- Technical validation: I’ve looped in Rishi for concurrency/streaming specifics.

If that lines up, we’ll follow with a formal SLA proposal and a DocuSign-ready redline for legal.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0136

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.pdf, slo-draft.docx

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We want both p95 and p99 called out in the SLA. p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms is our internal target.
- For streaming: we need first-byte latency <= 100ms, then steady streaming chunks with 30–60ms per chunk for clients on US East. Can Redwood provide region-specific numbers, or do we accept a global SLA with region-level reporting?
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows are fine; we’ll need to carve out our own load tests (we run 1h synthetic test monthly) — that should be excluded from SLA calculations.
- Reporting cadence: weekly dashboard is great, but legal will want monthly aggregated reports and an on-demand export for audits.
- Remedies: standard service credits are ok; proposal should include thresholds at 98%/95%/90% compliance bands.

We’re OK with Redwood drafting SLA language and the MAP — Priya will run legal/ops review once we see the draft.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of AI Platform, Acme Corp
samir.patel@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA language & measurement definitions (draft)

Samir / Priya —

Attached is the SLA proposal (sla-proposal.pdf) and a short summary below of the key measurement definitions and proposed remedies. Please review and let us know any redlines.

Measurement definitions (proposed):
- Measurement point: latency measured at Redwood service egress (i.e., time from request receipt by Redwood gateway to final token egress to client), excluding client-side network time.
- Metrics: p95 and p99 for single-shot generate; first-byte latency for streaming; average per-chunk egress time for streaming chunks after the first token.
- Windows & aggregation: rolling 30-day window for SLA compliance; daily aggregation for dashboarding; weekly and monthly exports available on request.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (with 72h prior notice), agreed-upon customer-initiated load tests (must be scheduled via MAP), force majeure, and validated upstream cloud provider outages.

Remedies (proposed):
- Service credits tiered by monthly compliance: <98% = 5% credit, <95% = 10% credit, <90% = 20% credit. Credits calculated on monthly platform fees for affected services.

Reporting cadence: weekly dashboard (token-level and latency breakdown) + monthly executive report (aggregated compliance, incidents, and root-cause summaries). Ad-hoc exports for audits available via support ticket.

Open items for technical confirmation from Rishi:
- Concurrency limits across model variants and how we surface per-model capacity in the console for Acme.
- Impact of KV cache warmup on first-byte latency for cold-start sequences.
- Whether streaming per-chunk numbers are feasible at 30–60ms across US-East under the requested concurrency.

I’ll incorporate any technical clarifications and produce a DocuSign-ready redline for legal once we align.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: sla-proposal.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language & measurement definitions (draft)

Marissa — quick technical notes for the SLA draft:

- Concurrency & throughput: For the Acme profile (avg 50-token responses, steady 120 req/s, bursts to 400 req/s), we recommend setting per-model soft concurrency target at 32 and a regional burst pool. The runtime can sustain bursts if requests are queued into the burst buffer; SLA applies to accepted requests — requests throttled by configured rate limits are not counted against SLA.
- Measurement specifics: measuring at egress (as proposed) is correct for customer-facing latency. We should explicitly call out that internal scheduling/queue time is included in the measurement (i.e., time spent waiting to be scheduled onto a GPU).
- KV cache warmup: cold sessions can add 100–300ms on first token depending on model size and quantization. Recommend an explicit exclusion for first-request cold-cache penalty in the first 10 minutes after model update or slot spin-up, or alternatively call out a separate cold-start metric that is excluded from SLA calculations.
- Streaming: 30–60ms per-chunk is achievable under ideal network conditions; to be conservative for SLA, propose first-byte <= 150ms and subsequent chunks <= 80ms as SLA targets for US regions, with optimistic internal targets of 100ms/40ms. Also note cross-region network variance — recommend region-specific reporting rather than per-region SLA unless Acme wants to buy region-specific commitments.

I can draft the technical addendum to the SLA with exact phrasing for exclusions and measurement points.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language & measurement definitions (draft)

Marissa / Rishi —

This looks good and aligns with our ops/legal expectations. A few quick asks:
- Please add the cold-start carve-out language Rishi suggested to the SLA doc.
- Can you provide region-level dashboards for US-East and US-West for the first month of the pilot?
- We’ll need a DocuSign-ready redline for legal — Priya from my team will own sign-off (cc’d Samir earlier).

Once those updates are in the draft, we’ll route to legal and procurement and aim to sign within two weeks.

Thanks —
Priya Shah
Director, AI Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
priya.shah@acme.com
